surveys.name: Redstone Camp Lookout
surveys.journal: From the tower the camp makes sense: the mule trail climbs north to The Overlook, and the county road drops east through the gullies to an old ranger station. A descent trail cuts down the draw below the tower.
surveys.next: Ranger Station, east down the county road (about 850 m).

surveys.name: Ranger Station Roof
surveys.journal: The survey disc on the roof still has its bearings. The creek crossing and a burned homestead lie south-east, and past them the road runs on to Ash Hollow, where a water tower stands above the flats.
surveys.next: Ash Hollow water tower, south-east along the county road.

surveys.name: Ash Hollow Water Tower
surveys.journal: From the tank catwalk you can see the county road run east out of the region, and a radio mast standing over Coyote Flats to the north. A windmill pump turns out on the prairie.
surveys.next: Coyote Flats radio mast, north along the county road.

surveys.name: Coyote Flats Radio Mast
surveys.journal: The relay log names a hunting cabin and a line shack to the north, both stocked before the ash came. Far to the west, on the highest ridge, the old fire lookout still catches the light.
surveys.next: The western fire lookout ruin, high on the far ridges (late).

surveys.name: Western Fire Lookout
surveys.journal: The whole country lies open from up here: every ridge trail, every road out. The region map is complete.

provenance: Procedural fallback terrain (not real DEM data). POIs fitted to the terrain from Anthony's map draft layout.
